$comment: Codex CLI on a ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business plan.
⛔ `cache.kind` was `unpriced` here until 2026-09-02, on the stated grounds that OpenAI
caching is 'automatic and server-side' with 'no TTL a scheduler can extend'. The first half
is true and the second half is not, and the difference is the whole file. Source: OpenAI
*Prompt caching* guide, read 2026-09-02.
A cached prefix on GPT-5.6 and later 'remains eligible for reuse for 30 minutes after its most
recent write or reuse', and 'reusing the prefix refreshes its lifetime without another
cache-write charge'. That is the same lever Anthropic sells, at half the length: a conversation
reused inside the window costs 0.1x and restarts its own clock, and one left past it costs
1.25x to rebuild. So `kind` is `ttl_multiplier`, exactly as in the Anthropic file - not a new
shape, just shorter and cheaper to rebuild.
⚠️ ONE 30m TTL COVERS ALL FOUR MODELS, and only the GPT-5.6 trio is documented at 30m.
gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-5.6-luna use `prompt_cache_options.ttl`, whose sole supported value is
'30m'. gpt-5.5 predates that and uses `prompt_cache_retention`, where the non-ZDR default '24h'
'typically keeps entries available for around 30 minutes and can retain them for up to 24 hours'.
Thirty minutes is therefore the honest number for all four: exact for the newer trio, and the
typical case for the older model. ⛔ It is NOT a floor for the older model - an organization with
Zero Data Retention enabled defaults to 'in_memory' instead, which
is '5 to 10 minutes of inactivity', and against that this file is optimistic. A ZDR fleet that
measures its own reuse rate should say so here rather than leave this comment standing.
⚠️ Cache writes cost 1.25x on GPT-5.6+ but nothing at all on the older model, and this file
charges every model the 1.25x. Erring toward the expensive side is the safe direction: it makes
the scheduler slightly too eager to reuse a warm prefix and slightly too reluctant to let one
lapse, and both of those fail toward reuse, which is free when the guess is wrong.
⭐ AND THIS FLEET'S OWN ROLLOUTS AGREE, which is worth recording because the paragraphs above
are read from a vendor page and this is measured on the machine. 2026-09-02, 331 consecutive
request pairs across 18 rollout JSONLs, comparing last_token_usage.cached_input_tokens against
the gap since the previous request: all 326 pairs under 5 minutes apart hit the cache, median
96.3% of the input served from it, single reads as large as 130,816 tokens. The five pairs over
10 hours apart all fell back to exactly 11,008 cached tokens - the static system/tool prefix -
with the conversation body cold. ⚠️ There is no sample between 5 minutes and 10 hours, so this
brackets the TTL only as (5m, 10h]: it corroborates the documented 30m and does not measure it.
The rollout field used is the same one probeQuota reads, so the check is free to repeat.
MODELS: refreshed from OpenAI's ChatGPT Codex model documentation on 2026-09-09 and verified live
with codex-cli 0.155.1 on 2026-09-20. ChatGPT-authenticated Codex supports `gpt-6-astra` (priority 1,
visibility: list, effort levels low through ultra) on ChatGPT Plus, Pro, and Business plans.
`gpt-5.4` and `gpt-5.4-mini` were retired for ChatGPT on 2026-08-31; `gpt-reserve` and `codex-auto-review`
remain omitted: the first is not an operator-routable model, and the second is the approval review agent.

cache.$comment: The 30m clock runs from the REQUEST that writes or reuses the prefix, not from the response that ends it - `ttl_measured_from` below, and the same correctness trap cost-model.md §1 records for Anthropic. A four-minute turn has already spent four of the thirty.

$comment: Codex has compaction in its session lifecycle, but no documented way to drive it from a
headless run. The adapter declares manualCompact: false deliberately - claiming a capability
that turns out to be absent strands a session at a window boundary, while omitting one that
is present costs only a missed optimisation.
⛔ This stays false even now that the cache is priced, and it is the reason Codex's clock is
a two-move clock where Anthropic's is a six-move one. With no way to shrink a conversation,
the only things worth doing with a warm codex prefix are to REUSE it inside the 30m window or
to LET IT LAPSE and start cold. `costOfCompact` returns null for this provider and every
compaction move is skipped on that alone.

$plans_comment: ⭐ THE FREE→PAID SWITCH IS READ FROM THE WINDOW SHAPE, NOT FROM THE IDENTITY STRING.
`auth.json` reports whatever the account is TODAY, which is a belief about now and says nothing
about a run from last week. The shape of the reading a run carried is evidence from the run
itself: measured 2026-09-02 over this install's own rows, every codex run up to 2026-09-01
21:28Z reports a single `30d` window (the free plan_type shape openai-compatible.ts documents)
and every run from 2026-09-02 03:46Z reports `5h` + `7d`. Eight runs on one side, sixteen on
the other, no overlap. So `detect` beats `match` wherever a run has its own reading.
⚠️ `default_plan` is `plus`, a PAID plan, deliberately. Defaulting to free would print `n/a`
over real money; defaulting to paid prints a number that is at worst too confident, and the
run's plan_source column says which it is.
